clue.text: Course director, virile type, inspiring old railway company

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the virile type takes the railway company inside him

parts.note: a he-man is a macho, virile fellow
the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, merged into British Railways in 1948

explanation.surface: A golf-course or racecourse manager, a macho man, takes on a historic railway firm as his inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course director' suggests a race or golf course; it is a ship's course. The LMS was a big British railway company before nationalisation in 1948.
explanation.definitionFit: The helmsman steers a vessel, so he directs its course over the water.

clue.text: Morse's last case calling up memories

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the detective's name is kept

parts.note: final letter of Morse
the vocative is a grammatical case, used in addressing someone

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse's final investigation brings back old memories for viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a detective's case for Morse; it is a grammatical case, as in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evocative summons up feelings and recollections, which is what calling up memories means.

clue.text: Chinatown's appalling nemesis?

indicators.note: something appalling is dreadfully messed up, so the letters that follow are put into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sly question whether some appalling foe threatens the Chinatown district of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinatown' must be split as 'china town': Meissen in Saxony is famous for its porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Meissen is the German town where European hard-paste porcelain, or china, was first made.

clue.text: Fruit consumed by some Londoners

indicators.note: what is consumed sits inside the eater, so the answer lies buried within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A kind of fruit that is eaten by a number of people in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a large juicy fruit such as a cantaloupe or watermelon.

clue.text: Clear obstruction in court?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to earn as profit after deductions
second meaning: the barrier across a tennis court

explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court and obstruction of justice; it is a tennis court, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To net a sum is to clear it as profit, and the net is the mesh barrier players hit over in tennis.

clue.text: Polluted air current breathed in by maternal grandmother

indicators.note: what is breathed in ends up inside the breather, so the current goes inside the grandmother

parts.note: your mother's mother is ma's ma
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Granny, on her mother's side, inhales a draught of dirty air.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside MA'S MA, after the first MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is an unpleasant or unhealthy vapour, foul-smelling and polluted atmosphere.

clue.text: Doctor working hard during function? That's eyewash!

indicators.note: during places one thing in the middle of another, so the hard letter sits within the function

parts.note: MO is medical officer, an army doctor
a machine that is on is working
sine is a trigonometric function
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A medic hard at work at some social event dismisses it all as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' suggests a party; it is a mathematical function.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for nonsense or humbug, talk not to be believed.

clue.text: Transport organisation's broadcast on policy

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
the party line is its policy; 'on' places this piece after the first

explanation.surface: A transport company's stated policy is put out over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An airline is a company that carries passengers and freight by aeroplane.

clue.text: Man securing root of tulip tree

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the man holds the kept letter within him

parts.note: a man is a male

indicators.note: in a down clue the root is the bottom, so the final letter of the flower is kept

parts.note: the last letter of tulip

explanation.surface: A gardener holds the root of a tulip tree, a real kind of tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The tulip tree is a real tree, which makes 'tulip tree' read as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a deciduous tree of the genus Acer, the source of maple syrup.

clue.text: Shot leaders of beasts in desert

parts.note: a go or shot is an attempt

indicators.note: leaders go in front, so the opening letters of the next words are taken

parts.note: first letter of beasts
first letter of in

explanation.surface: The lead animals of a herd are shot out in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: The leaders are of two words, 'beasts in', so 'in' gives a letter as well as reading as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is the great desert spanning Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: Pounds one quietly invested in new Hogarth print

parts.note: L is the sign for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so the soft letter goes within the rearranged name
a new version is a remade one, so the painter's name is rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
p, piano, is the musical mark for quietly

explanation.surface: Money is quietly put into a new print by the artist William Hogarth.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogarth was an 18th-century English painter and engraver, which makes 'print' fit the surface naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A lithograph is a print made by lithography, from an image drawn on stone or metal.

clue.text: Retired head plugging bleepers for travellers?

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole from inside, so the headland word goes within the bleepers

parts.note: pagers are bleepers, the beeping devices once carried by doctors

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the headland word runs the other way

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Orford Ness

explanation.surface: A retired headteacher fills a box with pagers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like an adjective for the head; it signals the reversal. The question mark covers the slightly loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers are the people carried on a journey who are not crew, so they are travellers.

clue.text: Voter shows muscle, changing sides almost at the start

indicators.text: changing sides almost at the start
indicators.note: sides are right and left, so near the front one side letter is swapped for the other

parts.note: an erector is a muscle that raises a body part

explanation.surface: A voter flexes their muscles, switching political sides just as a campaign starts.
explanation.walkthrough: In ERECTOR the R, second letter so almost at the start, becomes L: right becomes left.
explanation.definitionFit: An elector is a person entitled to vote in an election.

clue.text: Couple I encountered going west

indicators.note: in an across answer west is leftward, so the words are read from right to left

parts.note: encountered is met

explanation.surface: Someone recalls bumping into a pair of people heading west.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a couple in a romantic relationship, as in 'they are an item'.

clue.text: Austrian citizen struggles with English, going round North Tyneside

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so the struggles word wraps the compass letters

parts.note: vies is competes or struggles
standard abbreviation
Tyneside, around Newcastle, is in the North East of England
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An Austrian has difficulty with the English language when travelling around North Tyneside in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Viennese person lives in Vienna, Austria's capital, so is an Austrian citizen.

clue.text: Set aside, like some seals enclosing book

indicators.note: to enclose is to surround, so the seal word holds the book inside it

parts.note: eared seals, such as sea lions, have external ear flaps
Mark is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Something is put aside, sealed up like a document with a book inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seals' suggests wax seals on a document; they are the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark funds is to reserve or designate them for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Liberal leaving W African state for European peninsula

indicators.note: the party member leaves, so that letter departs from the country's name

parts.note: Liberia is on the west coast of Africa
standard abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician quits a West African country to move to Spain or Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the peninsula in south-west Europe shared by Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: Graceless modern worker supporting key cricket side

indicators.note: in a down answer a support sits underneath, so the worker is placed below the other pieces

parts.note: in means fashionable, up to date
E is a musical key
the leg side is one half of a cricket field, behind the batsman's legs
the worker ant, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A clumsy modern employee props up the most important side in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'supporting' puts the worker beneath the key and cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking grace or refinement, so clumsy and graceless.

clue.text: Condition ultimately discernible in her young cow

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the pronoun that follows

parts.note: taken as written
if introduces a condition

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of discernible

explanation.surface: Her condition is eventually noticeable in a young cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A heifer is a young female cow that has not yet borne a calf.

clue.text: Pay a grand: finally secure film material

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay it
taken as written
G is short for a grand, a thousand

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the last letter of secure

explanation.surface: Someone pays a thousand to finally get hold of some film.
explanation.definitionFit: Footage is recorded film or video, the raw material shot for a production.

clue.text: One who digs fish, extremely eager to protect river

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so the fish wraps around the river letter

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish
standard abbreviation

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters stay

parts.note: first and last letters of eager

explanation.surface: A digger who loves fish is keen to guard the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' suggests liking, so 'one who digs fish' reads as an angling fan; here it is literal digging.
explanation.definitionFit: A trencher is someone who digs trenches, so a digger by trade.

clue.text: Grant fencing in one type of tree

indicators.note: fencing in a field encloses it, so the grant word surrounds the numeral

parts.note: to confer an honour is to grant it
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grant pays for putting a fence around one particular kind of tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A conifer is a cone-bearing tree such as a pine or fir, one broad type of tree.

clue.text: Capital optimistic speculators laid out first of all

indicators.note: the first of all the words means each word's opening letter is taken

parts.note: initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Hopeful investors spent capital before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money for speculators; it is a capital city, Norway's.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Very fine cut, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so the word for cut is taken by its sound

parts.note: to shear is to cut, as with sheep's wool

explanation.surface: A very good cut of cloth, so people say.

clue.text: Unusually dark, a finer breed of cattle

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cattle breeder praises an unusually dark and superior breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Afrikander is a South African breed of red, humped cattle.

clue.text: Make obeisance naturally at first in ship

parts.note: first letter of naturally

explanation.surface: Someone bows down instinctively on first boarding a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To kneel is to go down on one's knees, a classic gesture of deference or obeisance.

clue.text: Outstanding, like schoolwork submitted a second time

definitions.meaning: first meaning: extraordinary, worthy of note

definitions.text: like schoolwork submitted a second time
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as re- plus markable: able to be marked again

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word as RE-MARKABLE, homework that can be graded once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable things are exceptional and striking, and the split reading means able to be assessed again.

clue.text: Sent up bill for American club

standard clothing-size abbreviation
